title: Wendell and the Colony
premise: Quentin Eriksen, a terraformer tending a garden on the dead world of Halcyon Reach, discovers her late mother's name forged onto the manifest of a colony ship that officially never launched. Digging into the forgery, she uncovers evidence that the ship's passengers—dissidents erased from every record—were massacred in orbit, and that the same corporate tribunal now rewriting history has marked Quentin herself for disappearance. With help from a disgraced archivist and a smuggler who owes her a debt, she races to recover the ship's black box before the garden she tends is 'reclaimed' and she vanishes like the others. In the end, Quentin broadcasts the truth from the colony's own seed-vault transmitter, trading her anonymity for justice, and chooses to stay on Halcyon as the first honest witness of its new beginning.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote stations in the high Arctic before turning to fiction. Her novels blend hard ecological detail with quiet, stubborn characters who refuse to let the past be paved over.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Quentin pilots the supply run between Halcyon Reach and the hub station Vespergate, cataloguing the silence between worlds that severed contact years ago. Third-person limited POV. Establishes her routine, her loneliness, and the garden she tends for colonists who may never come; ends with an odd ping from a decommissioned dock.

chapters.title: A Name That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Reviewing old manifests to justify a parts requisition, Quentin finds her mother Maren Eriksen listed as a passenger on the Meridian Dawn—a ship registered as never having flown. Her POV. The emotional beat is vertigo: grief reopening, suspicion kindling. She pockets the manifest chip before anyone notices.

chapters.title: Garden Logic
chapters.summary: Quentin tends the terraform terraces while turning the manifest over in her mind, testing it against everything she knows about records and rot. Her POV. A quiet chapter of denial giving way to resolve; she notices the registry database has been recently 'cleaned,' which no one admits to doing.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Fell
chapters.summary: On Vespergate, Quentin seeks out Ivo Sandoval, a former colonial archivist now selling salvage, who was fired for refusing to purge files. His POV. He recognizes the Meridian Dawn immediately and goes pale; he agrees to look at her chip but warns her that people who ask about it stop asking anything.

chapters.title: Forged in Good Faith
chapters.summary: Ivo authenticates the manifest: the forgery is recent, official-grade, and sloppy in exactly one field—the passenger count doesn't match life-support tonnage. Alternating POV. The beat is dread sharpening into purpose; they realize someone wanted Maren's name attached to a ghost ship deliberately.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Quentin realizes the forged name wasn't a mistake—it was a lure, meant to draw out anyone still carrying Eriksen family data. Her POV. Paranoia sets in as she spots a survey skiff shadowing her route home; she dumps false telemetry and takes the long way back to Halcyon.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Back on Halcyon, Quentin searches her mother's abandoned habitat module and finds a hidden cache: Maren's private logs referencing 'the passenger list' and a warning to trust no tribunal clerk. Her POV. Grief and anger fuse; the chapter ends with Maren's last line—'if you're reading this, they already erased us once.'

chapters.title: The Tribunal of Records
chapters.summary: Introduce antagonist: Auditor-General Corvane Hale of the Colonial Continuity Tribunal, reviewing a file flagged 'Eriksen.' His POV, cold and procedural. We learn the Tribunal exists to keep the colony narrative clean, and that Hale personally signed the erasure order eleven years ago. Beat: menace without malice.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Debt
chapters.summary: Quentin calls in a favor from Rhea Okonkwo, a smuggler whose life Quentin saved during a depressurization years ago. Rhea's POV. Reluctant alliance formed over bad coffee; Rhea agrees to ferry them to the debris belt where the Meridian Dawn allegedly never flew. Beat: wary trust.

chapters.title: Never Flown
chapters.summary: The trio reaches coordinates where orbital records show nothing, and finds a debris field—hull plating, cryo-shards, thousands of personal effects fused into slag. Quentin's POV. Horror lands physically; she finds a child's shoe with a serial number matching the manifest. Beat: the massacre becomes real.

chapters.title: Black Box Doctrine
chapters.summary: Ivo explains the flight recorder must be intact somewhere in the field—the Tribunal never recovered it because admitting the search meant admitting the ship. His POV. Hope rekindles; they plan a salvage dive under cover of a meteor survey. Beat: fragile strategy against overwhelming odds.

chapters.title: Hale Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Hale learns a salvage beacon pinged inside the restricted debris zone and authorizes a 'sanitation team.' His POV. We see his logic: not cruelty, but tidiness. Beat: cold escalation; he orders Quentin's garden permit revoked, making her legally invisible within days.

chapters.title: The Dive
chapters.summary: Rhea and Quentin suit up into the debris field while Ivo runs interference on comms. Quentin's POV. Claustrophobic tension among drifting dead; she locates the recorder housing wedged in the engine section. Beat: triumph cut short when a sanitation cutter arrives early.

chapters.title: Running Silent
chapters.summary: A chase through the debris belt as Rhea threads the freighter through wreckage with sanitation guns firing. Rhea's POV. Adrenaline chapter; they escape with the black box but take hull damage and lose their comm relay. Beat: survival at cost—they're stranded, dark, and hunted.

chapters.title: Voices in the Box
chapters.summary: In deep space, they crack the recorder: final forty minutes of the Meridian Dawn, including passengers' pleas and a Tribunal order to vent the decks. Quentin's POV. Devastation and fury; she hears her mother's voice refusing to give up names. Beat: grief transmuted into testimony.

chapters.title: What Maren Knew
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing the recorder with Maren's logs, Ivo reconstructs why: the passengers were dissidents who discovered the terraforming program was a land-grab fraud, and the massacre protected the claim. Ivo's POV. Beat: the crime is bigger than murder—it's theft of a world.

chapters.title: Sanctioned Silence
chapters.summary: Hale receives confirmation the recorder is missing and faces his superiors, who instruct him to burn Halcyon's atmosphere certification rather than risk exposure. His POV. First crack in his certainty—he hesitates over the order. Beat: the antagonist begins to feel the weight of what tidy means.

chapters.title: Stranded Light
chapters.summary: Damaged and dark, the crew limps toward a derelict waystation to repair. Rhea's POV. Quiet interlude: campfire-in-space intimacy, confessions about what each lost to the colonies. Beat: found-family bonds solidify before the storm.

chapters.title: The Waystation's Ghosts
chapters.summary: In the waystation archives, Ivo finds pre-erasure colony charts proving the land-grab fraud independently of the recorder. His POV. They now hold two proofs—but also realize the Tribunal will torch Halcyon to bury both. Beat: victory curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Reclamation Notice
chapters.summary: Quentin receives automated notice: Halcyon Reach will be 'atmospherically reset' in nine days, all assets forfeit. Her POV. The garden she tended for the unborn will be sterilized—and her with it if she stays. Beat: the clock starts loudly.

chapters.title: Nine Days of Green
chapters.summary: Quenton returns alone to Halcyon to save the garden's seed vault, the only structure hardened enough to survive a reset—and home to the colony's original transmitter array. Her POV. Tender, elegiac work among living things she may be saying goodbye to. Beat: love of place as motivation.

chapters.title: Hale Descends
chapters.summary: Hale personally travels to Halcyon to oversee the reset, expecting a paperwork errand, and walks the terraces Quentin built. His POV. Unsettled by the garden's beauty and by a plaque bearing names he ordered erased. Beat: conscience knocking.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Nursery
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts Hale directly among the seedlings, playing him thirty seconds of the recorder audio. Both POVs interleaved. He doesn't deny it; he says 'the alternative was chaos.' Beat: moral collision—justice versus order, neither cleanly right.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Hale offers Quentin reinstatement, a new identity, and the garden's survival if she surrenders the recorder. Her POV. She asks for one night to decide; he grants it, telling himself it's procedure. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Night of Seeds
chapters.summary: Quentin spends the night planting the vault with everything the garden holds, deciding what deserves to outlive her. Her POV. Meditative climax-of-will chapter; she resolves that inheritance means truth, not soil. Beat: quiet steel.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: At dawn Quentin refuses Hale's offer and triggers the vault's lockdown. Her POV. Hale, bound by his own rules, cannot shoot without witnesses—so he seals the facility and waits for the reset fleet. Beat: checkmate seemingly against her.

chapters.title: Rhea's Gambit
chapters.summary: Rhea flies the damaged freighter straight at the reset fleet broadcasting a fake distress as a colony ship in peril, forcing an emergency halt to the atmospheric strike. Rhea's POV. Audacious, near-suicidal diversion. Beat: courage buying minutes.

chapters.title: The Seed-Vault Transmitter
chapters.summary: Inside the vault, Quentin and Ivo jury-rig the original colony transmitter to broadcast the recorder audio, the fraud charts, and the passenger names across every open channel. Ivo's POV. Race-against-the-clock engineering under failing power. Beat: hope assembled from scraps.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The truth goes out: forty minutes of the Meridian Dawn's final moments, heard on Vespergate, on the hub, on the reset fleet itself. Multiple brief POVs of ordinary people hearing it. Beat: the erased become un-erasable in real time.

chapters.title: Fleet in Revolt
chapters.summary: Reset fleet crews refuse the strike order; captains demand verification from the Tribunal, which can no longer produce records fast enough to lie coherently. Ensemble POV. Beat: institutional collapse under the weight of witnessed truth.

chapters.title: Hale's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to destroy the vault and everyone in it, Hale instead transmits his own authentication codes confirming the erasure order's signature—his own. His POV. Not redemption, but refusal to compound the crime. Beat: the antagonist breaks the machine from inside.

chapters.title: Siege of the Vault
chapters.summary: Tribunal loyalists assault the seed vault; Quentin, Ivo, and arriving Rhea defend the transmitter room in a desperate last stand. Quentin's POV. Action climax; Ivo is gravely wounded shielding the uplink. Beat: everything paid for at once.

chapters.title: Ceasefire Among the Seedlings
chapters.summary: Vespergate marshals arrive with arrest warrants—not for Quentin, but for the Tribunal council—as fighting stops mid-breach. Ensemble POV. Beat: the law finally arrives, late and borrowed, to do what justice outside the law already did.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Quentin gives formal testimony, naming every passenger on the Meridian Dawn aloud into the record so each enters legal existence again. Her POV. Cathartic, ceremonial chapter; she speaks her mother's name last. Beat: grief given a public shape.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Names
chapters.summary: Memorial observances across the colonies; families Quentin never knew contact her with fragments of the erased to be archived. Ivo, recovering, begins rebuilding the colonial archive properly. His POV. Beat: restoration as slow collective work.

chapters.title: The Question of Staying
chapters.summary: Offered a post on Vespergate and full reinstatement, Quentin weighs leaving Halcyon forever. Her POV. Rhea offers her a berth; the garden offers her roots. Beat: belonging chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hale, awaiting trial, requests one visitor: Quentin. Their final conversation about whether order can ever be innocent. Dual POV. He asks her to tend the memorial grove where the reset was cancelled. Beat: uneasy, human closure.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.summary: Quentin opens the seed vault publicly and leads the first true planting on Halcyon—colonists, survivors' kin, and the formerly erased honored row by row. Her POV. Joyful, grounded chapter. Beat: the garden finally has its people.

chapters.title: The Manifest, Corrected
chapters.summary: The official record of the Meridian Dawn is rewritten in truth: launched, boarded, murdered, mourned. Quentin files the corrected manifest herself, adding one line—'witnessed by Q. Eriksen, gardener.' Her POV. Beat: inheritance fulfilled on paper and in spirit.

chapters.title: Wendell Blooms
chapters.summary: Epilogue a year later: the first orchard blossoms on Halcyon, named Wendell after the child whose shoe Quentin found in the debris. Her POV, watching ships arrive that speak to each other again. Final beat: staying visible, staying rooted, the future finally invited to arrive.
